Fuel costs

When calculating how much fuel to use in a firepit , consider the following:

  • Rearranging the contents of a cooking pot or crucible into 1 slot or 4 slots makes no difference.
  • The speed at which the firepit heats up will decrease when there is a larger quantity in the input slot—a stack of items, a cooking pot with many servings, or a crucible with many nuggets.
  • When a stack of items reaches its required temperature, it will begin cooking or smelting one by one. The speed increases with higher temperatures.
  • When a container reaches its required temperature, it will begin cooking or smelting all at once. The speed increases with higher temperatures, and decreases with a larger quantity of contents.
  • All metals smelt at the same speed at their respective melting temperature. However, it is easier to achieve excessively high temperatures for metals with a lower melting point.

Alternative fuels

Other organic matter and crafted items, such as baskets and furniture, can also be used as less efficient fuel in a firepit.
